notes: v2.5.14 - required update. Quality & AS9100: the Risk module has been rebuilt to the specification the quality team asked for. Risks are now scored on Severity and Frequency on a 1-25 scale, with Frequency optional, and Detection and RPN have been removed. Categories, source/trigger and current control are pick-lists of real, plain-English options instead of free text, only a category and a description are required to raise a risk, and there is now one badge scan instead of two. Every existing risk has been re-banded onto the new scale; nothing has been deleted. Inventory: Physical Inventory is split into three tabs - project stock, consumables and unclassified - with a proper worklist for stock nobody has classified yet, consumables shown as the received lots they actually are with readable names, and columns that now stay blank rather than state a figure they cannot know. Each lot carries its own editable Lot Description alongside the read-only Part Description, and both are searchable. Sourcing & Stock - the quantities now match the shelf: on-hand on the materials list is a real calculated figure instead of zero, available versus allocated is worked out from genuine commitments so fully-spoken-for material stops appearing available, shortages count what has already been consumed instead of raising phantom shortfalls, and stock that arrived before a vendor part was linked to a material is adopted the moment the link is made. Receiving can now point a part at a material that already exists or create a project material rather than only creating something new, the unclassified-parts backlog is on the dashboard, material names follow one rule everywhere, and the Vendor Parts tab leads through to the part instead of being a dead end. Purchasing: the vendor picker is 851 names shorter - vendors with no order, requisition or receipt since 2020 have been retired from the pickers, taking the selectable list from 2,065 to 1,214. Nothing historical changes and any of them can be reinstated. CATIA remote viewing: a machine is now released however the session ends - a crash, a power cut, quitting the app or closing the stream window - not only when you press Disconnect, and abandoned queue places are cleared, so machines stop reading as permanently claimed while nobody is on them. Waiting in the queue no longer looks like a disconnection. The stream window closes properly, full screen genuinely fills the screen with no second taskbar, CATIA no longer fights you for the mouse and keyboard, the remote machines have an orange taskbar so you always know which desktop you are looking at, the session controls have moved off the video and into the AOS streaming panel, you can pick which machine to connect to and queue for that specific machine, and copy and paste works in both directions. Workforce planner: every build that is in progress now appears, including builds with no hours budgeted, hovering a build shows its hours, dates, schedule position and department problems, departments over capacity or out of window are flagged on the build itself, the build hours screen is a compact table, a department with no capacity recorded reads as "no data" instead of a crisis, and the page no longer dims every few minutes while you are reading it. Project hours accuracy: time now follows the job code people clock into, so hours land on the project the work was actually done for rather than being credited to the wrong one - some projects will show hours that were previously credited elsewhere or not showing at all. Access: creating and editing materials and vendor-part links is now limited to the people who do that work; shop-floor actions - adjusting, consuming, outlife and splitting - are deliberately unchanged for everyone. Also: the retired Project Tracker page has been removed, Inventory's pop-ups all share one consistent look, and there are various fixes to project date handling and hours reporting. This release also updates the database behind AOS, so please update as soon as you are prompted.
